**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (40 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity. You should write between 450 - 500 words.

questions.enonce_markdown: **d)** Distance learning should be practised in Cameroon. Do you agree?
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Introduction: define distance learning and state the position (agree, with conditions).
2. Argument 1: it reaches pupils in remote areas and gives flexibility.
3. Argument 2: it saves cost and keeps schooling going during crises (strikes, insecurity, pandemic).
4. Counter-argument: poor electricity, internet and gadgets; reply with solutions.
5. Conclusion: restate agreement.

**Model composition (458 words)**

Distance learning is a method of education in which the teacher and the learner are in different places and communicate through radio, television, the internet or printed materials. Some people think that it cannot work in Cameroon. I strongly believe, however, that it should be practised in our country, provided that the government and the schools prepare it well.

The first reason is that distance learning brings education to those who are far from good schools. In many villages of the North, the East and the Far North, pupils walk several kilometres to reach a school with only one or two teachers. If lessons are broadcast on radio or recorded on a flash drive, a pupil in such a village can listen to the same quality of teaching as a child in Yaounde or Douala. Likewise, adults who work during the day, young mothers and school drop-outs can study in the evening and obtain a certificate without leaving their families.

The second reason is that distance learning saves money and keeps schooling alive in difficult times. A parent who sends a child to a boarding school pays for transport, accommodation and feeding. With online or radio lessons, much of that expense disappears. Moreover, our country has lived through teachers' strikes, insecurity in some regions and the COVID-19 pandemic. Each time, thousands of children lost months of teaching. Where distance learning was available, even in a small way, they kept learning.

Critics argue that Cameroon does not have regular electricity, cheap internet or enough phones and computers, and that many parents cannot afford them. This objection is serious, but it is not final. Radio is cheap, and almost every home owns a set. The government can also give priority to solar-powered community learning centres, reduce the price of data for educational websites and train teachers to prepare lessons for different media. Furthermore, face-to-face meetings can be organised during the holidays to help weak students and to supervise practical work. In this way, the difficulties will gradually be solved.

Another worry is that pupils may not be disciplined enough to study alone. This is true, but discipline can be taught. Timetables, regular assignments and phone calls from tutors will help learners to remain committed. Pupils who study alone also learn to manage their own time, a skill that is useful for the rest of their lives. After all, many successful people in the world studied by correspondence.

In conclusion, distance learning is not a replacement for classrooms, but it is a powerful partner. It reaches the unreachable, reduces cost and protects education in times of crisis. For these reasons, I fully agree that it should be practised in Cameroon, and I urge the authorities to invest in it without delay.

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 12 | A clear position, at least two developed arguments, a counter-argument with a reply, and a conclusion |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, a style and tone suited to the topic, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Giving a list of opinions without a clear position or without examples from Cameroon.
2. Ignoring the opposing view, or writing a narrative instead of an argument.
